title: Accessible error summaries and field-level errors
learningObjectives: Explain accessible error summaries and field-level errors and create accessible, secure form behaviour.

understand.concept: Accessible form errors identify the field, explain the problem in text, and help users move to the relevant control. An error summary can link to invalid fields; field-level messages can be associated using aria-describedby and invalid state can be conveyed with aria-invalid when appropriate.
understand.whyItMatters: Users need to understand what went wrong and how to fix it. Do not rely on colour alone, and manage focus carefully after submission so keyboard and screen-reader users can find the summary or first error.
understand.analogy: An error summary is a map of problems; each field message gives the precise instruction for fixing one location.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual validation, submission, and assistive technology behaviour follow browser and platform rules.

explain.narrative: The summary links to the field, and the field references its own explanatory message. Production behaviour should update errors based on actual validation state.

practise.guidedTask: Build a form with two invalid fields. Add an error summary with links, field-level messages, aria-describedby, and sensible focus handling after submit.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form with labels, constraints, clear errors, and a documented server-side validation plan. Test keyboard use and invalid values.
hints: Do not rely on colour or placeholder alone.
Client-side checks do not provide authorization or security.
Keep errors associated with their fields and easy to locate.

questions.answer: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.explanation: Good forms combine user-friendly browser feedback with trusted server-side enforcement.
